messages:
sailfish-dev: Hi CS, onboarding Sailfish app. After integrating @redwood/sdk v0.10, we see many 429s on first run across QA devices. No real traffic.

sailfish-dev: Log excerpt:
```
2026-05-02T08:00:00Z preflight GET 200
2026-05-02T08:00:00Z POST /v1/handshake 401 auth_missing
2026-05-02T08:00:00Z POST /v1/handshake 429 rate_limit:preflight
2026-05-02T08:00:01Z POST /v1/handshake 429 rate_limit:preflight
```

jenny_cs: sounds like multiple processes are racing to fetch ephemeral tokens then retrying. What's your token TTL and how many inits on startup?

sailfish-dev: TTL=30s. App spawns worker + main process; both call `init()` concurrently.

rick_se: classic fanout. Short TTL + parallel init -> stampede. Quick fixes: 1) centralize token fetch (single-source), 2) add small init splay (100-500ms), 3) client-side rate-limited retry/backoff. Example config:
```
Redwood.init({ preflightConcurrency:1, preflightSplayMs: 200 + Math.random()*300, retry: { baseMs:200, maxMs:2000 } })
```

infra-bot: Applied temporary preflight QPS increase to 50 for account sailfish-inc until 2026-05-03T08:00:00Z. Monitor dashboards.

rate-monitor: Alert: preflight 429 spike detected for sailfish-inc; suggested interventions: increase TTL during onboarding, serialize token fetch, reduce parallel inits.

sailfish-dev: implemented splay + single-token-broker + backoff. Re-tested with 12 devices parallel: transient 1-2 429s, otherwise stable. Thanks.

jenny_cs: follow-ups: sailfish to paste token broker snippet, Redwood to send preflight best-practices doc, infra to auto-revert quota bump. I'll schedule 15-min enablement.

sailfish-dev: will post snippet and confirm demo tomorrow morning. :thumbsup:
